subject: Draft: Private VPC runbook + reference diagrams (control plane / data plane separation)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julie Park <julie.park@acme-health.com>, DevOps Team <devops_ops@acme-health.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Private VPC runbook + reference diagrams (control plane / data plane separation)

Team,

Attached is the first draft of the Private VPC runbook we agreed to share with Acme Health. The focus here is the control plane / data plane separation, network zoning, and minimal egress patterns for air-gapped-friendly installs. Key asks:

- Karthik: quick pass on the control plane API ports and auth flows (Section 3).
- Mina: review the KV-cache persistence and S3 gateway notes (Section 5).
- Markus: operational checklist and rollback steps—please add anything missing.
- Julie / Acme: any initial concerns on the network diagrams or compliance notes?

Files attached: redwood-private-vpc-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook), controlplane-dataplane-seq-diagram.png, egress-proxy-config-snippets.txt

High-level notes in the runbook:
- Control plane lives in a subnet with no internet egress by default; we allow restricted outbound to our control-plane telemetry endpoints via a managed NAT in the customer account.
- Data plane (GPU serving) is isolated to a separate VPC peered via private VPC attachment; only the control plane subnet can signal model rollouts.
- Optional on-prem edge proxy for environments where direct peering is not allowed (diagram on page 4).
- Suggested canary window and traffic fraction for model rollouts (section 7).

Please review by EOD Monday so we can consolidate and send to Acme legal/security.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: Private VPC runbook + reference diagrams (control plane / data plane separation)

Neha — thanks for pulling this together. Quick notes after a pass on Section 3 (control plane):

- Port/endpoint matrix: please add port 8443 TCP for the control-plane admin API (we use mTLS). I added an inline note in the runbook PDF.
- Auth flow: recommend we explicitly call out client-cert rotation cadence (90 days) and reference our KMS-integration doc; otherwise the customer FAQ will ping us for that.
- Telemetry egress: for customers who can't permit NAT outbound, add a scheduling option to batch telemetry uploads via an on-prem relay (low frequency, queued).

Minor: the control-plane IAM snippet uses a broad role; suggest tightening to a service-role-with-deny-list for S3 buckets that contain customer data in other projects.

I'll send a PR to the runbook with these edits.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Neha / all — good draft. A couple operational additions from my side:

- Rollback checklist: include an explicit step to revoke model-signing keys and revert traffic routing at the LB level (this is critical for customer-facing models).
- Canary monitoring: add a short list of SLOs we measure during canary (latency P95, error % by model signature, token throughput).
- Postmortem hooks: if a rollout is reversed, require a joint postmortem within 72 hours (owner: Acme SRE + Redwood on-call).

I'll add these to a new section and push to the shared Drive link. Also, Mina — please confirm that the KV persistence recommendation (flush-to-S3 window) matches our current LRU eviction behavior.

Markus Klein
Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

Neha / team — thanks for the thorough draft. A few items from Acme's side:

- The separation model looks good to our network team; we will need the finalized port/endpoint matrix (Karthik's note) to put into our change window request.
- On telemetry egress: we prefer the batch/relay approach (our policy forbids continuous outbound to third-party telemetry endpoints). Can you add an example config and retention spec?
- Compliance ask: can you confirm the default data retention policy in the runbook (we saw a 30-day cache flush note — we need confirmation that's configurable to 7/30/90 days).

Next steps: if you can send an updated PDF with the port matrix and a brief config example for the telemetry relay, we'll prepare a scoped change request and propose a maintenance window next week.

Thanks,
Julie Park
Senior Infrastructure Manager
Acme Health
